claim: In the inner plexiform layer (IPL) of the mouse retina, ~70 neuronal subtypes organize their neurites into an intricate laminar structure that underlies visual processing.
source: In the inner plexiform layer (IPL) of the mouse retina, ~70 neuronal subtypes organize their neurites into an intricate laminar structure that underlies visual processing.
evidence: This is a statement about the structural organization of the mouse retina IPL, drawing from established knowledge in the field.

claim: The study utilized microarray data from 13 subtypes to identify differentially-expressed extracellular proteins.
source: To find recognition proteins involved in lamination, we utilized microarray data from 13 subtypes to identify differentially-expressed extracellular proteins and performed a high-throughput biochemical screen.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The study performed a high-throughput biochemical screen.
source: To find recognition proteins involved in lamination, we utilized microarray data from 13 subtypes to identify differentially-expressed extracellular proteins and performed a high-throughput biochemical screen.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The study identified ~50 previously-unknown receptor-ligand pairs.
source: We identified ~50 previously-unknown receptor-ligand pairs, including new interactions among members of the FLRT and Unc5 families.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the biochemical screen reported in the manuscript.

claim: New interactions among members of the FLRT and Unc5 families were identified.
source: We identified ~50 previously-unknown receptor-ligand pairs, including new interactions among members of the FLRT and Unc5 families.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the biochemical screen reported in the manuscript.

claim: FLRT and Unc5 proteins show laminar-restricted IPL localization.
source: These proteins show laminar-restricted IPL localization and induce attraction and/or repulsion of retinal neurites in culture, placing them in an ideal position to mediate laminar targeting.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data presented in the manuscript.

claim: FLRT and Unc5 proteins induce attraction and/or repulsion of retinal neurites in culture.
source: These proteins show laminar-restricted IPL localization and induce attraction and/or repulsion of retinal neurites in culture, placing them in an ideal position to mediate laminar targeting.
evidence: This is supported by stripe assay experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: FLRT and Unc5 proteins are in an ideal position to mediate laminar targeting.
source: These proteins show laminar-restricted IPL localization and induce attraction and/or repulsion of retinal neurites in culture, placing them in an ideal position to mediate laminar targeting.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization and functional data presented.

claim: FLRT2 and Unc5C exhibit complementary expression patterns in vivo.
source: Consistent with a repulsive role in arbor lamination, we observed complementary expression patterns for one interaction pair, FLRT2-Unc5C, in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing expression patterns in retinal sections.

claim: Starburst amacrine cells express FLRT2.
source: Starburst amacrine cells and their synaptic partners, ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells, express FLRT2 and are repelled by Unc5C.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and immunostaining data on cultured SACs.

claim: ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells express FLRT2.
source: Starburst amacrine cells and their synaptic partners, ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells, express FLRT2 and are repelled by Unc5C.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization and stripe assay data on Drd4-GFP neurons.

claim: Starburst amacrine cells are repelled by Unc5C.
source: Starburst amacrine cells and their synaptic partners, ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells, express FLRT2 and are repelled by Unc5C.
evidence: This is supported by stripe assay experiments showing SAC repulsion by Unc5C.

claim: ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells are repelled by Unc5C.
source: Starburst amacrine cells and their synaptic partners, ON-OFF direction-selective ganglion cells, express FLRT2 and are repelled by Unc5C.
evidence: This is supported by stripe assay experiments on Drd4-GFP neurons.

claim: A single molecular mechanism may have been co-opted by synaptic partners to ensure joint laminar restriction.
source: These data suggest a single molecular mechanism may have been co-opted by synaptic partners to ensure joint laminar restriction.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data regarding FLRT2-Unc5C interactions in SACs and DSGCs.

claim: The IPL is a stratified neuropil composed of axons and dendrites belonging to ~70 different subtypes of neurons.
source: The inner plexiform layer (IPL) of the retina is a stratified neuropil composed of axons and dendrites belonging to ~70 different subtypes of neurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about retinal structure cited in the introduction.

claim: IPL neurons synapse selectively on specific partners, forming a complex set of parallel circuits.
source: These neurons synapse selectively on specific partners, forming a complex set of parallel circuits, so a high degree of specificity is required during the wiring process (for review see Sanes and Zipursky, 2010; Hoon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited review articles.

claim: A high degree of specificity is required during the wiring process in the IPL.
source: These neurons synapse selectively on specific partners, forming a complex set of parallel circuits, so a high degree of specificity is required during the wiring process (for review see Sanes and Zipursky, 2010; Hoon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference from the complexity of IPL circuits, supported by cited reviews.

claim: Three major classes of neurons (bipolar, amacrine, and retinal ganglion cells) form connections with each other in five IPL synaptic sublayers, termed S1-S5.
source: Three major class of neurons (bipolar, amacrine, and retinal ganglion cells (RGCs)) form connections with each other in five IPL synaptic sublayers, termed S1-S5 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is established knowledge about IPL organization, also illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Most IPL neurons project selectively to just one or a few sublayers.
source: Most neurons project selectively to just one or a few of these sublayers.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IPL neuron targeting patterns.

claim: The Mouse Genome 430 2.0 microarray contains 45,101 probeset IDs.
source: The Mouse Genome 430 2.0 microarray (Affymetrix, CA) contains 45,101 probeset IDs.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the microarray platform used, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 35,469 probeset IDs have UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot identifiers and correspond to protein-encoding genes.
source: Of these, 35,469 have UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot identifiers and, as such, correspond to protein-encoding genes.
evidence: This is a result from the bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Protein sequences were submitted to SignalP server to predict the presence of a signal peptide.
source: Protein sequences were submitted to the SignalP server which predicts the presence of a signal peptide (Petersen et al., 2011) and the TMHMM server which predicts the presence of a transmembrane domain (Krogh et al., 2001).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methodology used, with citations to the tools.

claim: Protein sequences were submitted to TMHMM server to predict the presence of a transmembrane domain.
source: Protein sequences were submitted to the SignalP server which predicts the presence of a signal peptide (Petersen et al., 2011) and the TMHMM server which predicts the presence of a transmembrane domain (Krogh et al., 2001).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methodology used, with citations to the tools.

claim: The study identified ~200 genes encoding extracellular proteins that exhibited ≥3-fold difference in microarray expression levels amongst the neuronal subtypes.
source: We identified ~200 genes encoding extracellular proteins that exhibited ≥3-fold difference in microarray expression levels amongst the neuronal subtypes.
evidence: This is a result from the microarray differential expression analysis.

claim: 65 genes were selected as primary candidates based on domains and known players in cell-cell recognition.
source: Based on the domains present in each protein and known players involved in cell-cell recognition, we selected 65 genes as primary candidates and cloned them from retinal cDNA (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the candidate selection process.

claim: The 65 primary candidate genes comprised 121 distinct cDNAs, including 15 splice variants that have not been previously reported.
source: Because many of the genes encode more than one protein isoform as a result of alternative splicing or proteolytic cleavage, these primary candidates comprised 121 distinct cDNAs, including 15 splice variants that have not been previously reported (Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the cloning and characterization of candidate genes.

claim: New splice variants were identified for Ncam1, Netrin5, several Semaphorins and all four Unc5s.
source: New splice variants were identified for Ncam1, Netrin5, several Semaphorins and all four Unc5s (i.e. Unc5A-D).
evidence: This is a result from the cloning and characterization of candidate genes.

claim: The candidate proteins fall into three categories: secreted (26/121; 22%), GPI-linked (17/121; 14%) and type I transmembrane (78/121; 64%).
source: The candidate proteins fall into three categories: secreted (26/121; 22%), GPI-linked (17/121; 14%) and type I transmembrane (78/121; 64%).
evidence: This is a categorization of the candidate proteins based on their structural features.

claim: For AP-tagged proteins, 106 out of 121 (88%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations.
source: For AP-tagged proteins, 106 out of 121 (88%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations; for Fc-tagged proteins, 110 out of 121 (91%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations (see Materials and methods) (Figure 1—source data 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the recombinant protein production, with supporting Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: For Fc-tagged proteins, 110 out of 121 (91%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations.
source: For AP-tagged proteins, 106 out of 121 (88%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations; for Fc-tagged proteins, 110 out of 121 (91%) proteins were produced at optimal concentrations (see Materials and methods) (Figure 1—source data 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the recombinant protein production, with supporting Western blot data in supplementary figures.

claim: Interactions at the cell surface exhibit low affinities (KD ~ µM) and fast dissociation rates.
source: It is largely the case that interactions at the cell surface exhibit low affinities (KD ~ µM) and fast dissociation rates (Vandermerwe and Barclay, 1994), kinetic properties that allow transient, contact-dependent interactions to occur between recognition proteins expressed on neighboring cells in vivo but often make biochemical detection in vitro difficult.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell surface protein interactions, supported by a citation.

claim: The ELISA-based binding assay tetramerizes the AP-tagged receptor and Fc-tagged ligand proteins.
source: Our ELISA-based binding assay surmounts this limitation because it utilizes a strategy that tetramerizes the AP-tagged receptor and Fc-tagged ligand proteins (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes a key feature of the assay methodology.

claim: By inducing tetramers, the assay is highly sensitive allowing proteins with micromolar affinities to be detected at nanomolar concentrations.
source: By inducing tetramers, which provides additive or avidity effects, the assay is highly sensitive allowing proteins with micromolar affinities to be detected at nanomolar concentrations.
evidence: This explains the sensitivity advantage of the tetramerization strategy.

claim: The study tested 126 proteins for binding in a matrix which reciprocally tests every pair-wise combination (126 x 126 = 15,876 binding reactions).
source: We tested the 126 proteins for binding in a matrix which reciprocally tests every pair-wise combination (i.e. 126 x 126 = 15,876 binding reactions) (Figure 2; Visser et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the scale of the binding screen, with results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The screen includes 126 homophilic pairs and 7,875 unique heterophilic pairs.
source: This includes 126 homophilic pairs and 7,875 unique heterophilic pairs.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the matrix design.

claim: Interacting proteins were defined as those that exhibited ≥5-fold binding above background levels.
source: Interacting proteins identified in the screen were defined as those that exhibited ≥5-fold binding above background levels.
evidence: This describes the threshold used to identify positive interactions.

claim: The study identified 192 unique interaction pairs.
source: Using this criteria, we identified 192 unique interaction pairs, ~50 of which, to our knowledge, have not been reported in the literature (Figure 3 and Figure 4; Visser et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a primary result from the binding screen.

claim: Of 109 expected positive control interaction pairs, 91 were identified, giving a false negative rate of 17%.
source: Of these 109 positive control interaction pairs, we identified 91 giving us a false negative rate of 17%.
evidence: This is an assessment of the screen's sensitivity based on known interactions.

claim: The false negative rate of 17% is lower than published values for yeast-two-hybrid screens which give rise to false negative rates between 28 and 51%.
source: This frequency is lower than published values for the yeast-two-hybrid screen which gives rise to false negative rates between 28 and 51% (Huang and Bader, 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison to another screening method, supported by a citation.

claim: All three FLRT (FLRT1-3) and all four Unc5 (Unc5A-D) family members exhibited interactions in the screen.
source: Interactions between all three FLRT (FLRT1-3) and all four Unc5 (Unc5A-D) family members were observed in the screen; and all pairs exhibited high levels of binding at or near the level of saturation of detection (mean Abs650nm value = 2.14).
evidence: This is a result from the binding screen.

claim: All FLRT-Unc5 pairs exhibited high levels of binding at or near the level of saturation of detection (mean Abs650nm value = 2.14).
source: Interactions between all three FLRT (FLRT1-3) and all four Unc5 (Unc5A-D) family members were observed in the screen; and all pairs exhibited high levels of binding at or near the level of saturation of detection (mean Abs650nm value = 2.14).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the binding screen.

claim: Prior to the screen, four FLRT-Unc5 interactions had been described in the literature (three in mouse and one in zebrafish).
source: Furthermore, of the 12 possible FLRT-Unc5 interactions (i.e. 3 FLRTs x 4 Unc5s), prior to our screen, four had been described in the literature (three in mouse and one in zebrafish) (Karaulanov et al., 2009; Sollner and Wright, 2009; Yamagishi et al., 2011) suggesting that the eight new FLRT-Unc5 binding pairs we identified were likely to represent biologically-relevant interactions rather than false positives.
evidence: This is a literature review statement supported by citations.

claim: The study identified eight new FLRT-Unc5 binding pairs.
source: Furthermore, of the 12 possible FLRT-Unc5 interactions (i.e. 3 FLRTs x 4 Unc5s), prior to our screen, four had been described in the literature (three in mouse and one in zebrafish) (Karaulanov et al., 2009; Sollner and Wright, 2009; Yamagishi et al., 2011) suggesting that the eight new FLRT-Unc5 binding pairs we identified were likely to represent biologically-relevant interactions rather than false positives.
evidence: This is a result from the binding screen, inferred from the total possible interactions minus previously known ones.

claim: Concentration-dependent binding curves were observed for all FLRT-Unc5 interactions tested in titration experiments.
source: In all cases, we observed concentration-dependent binding curves.
evidence: This is a result from titration binding experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The FLRT-Unc5 binding constants observed in titration curves (on the order of ~1–10 nM) are much higher than published affinities using monomeric protein in surface plasmon resonance experiments (0.3-21 μM).
source: Because the extracellular region of the proteins used in these titration curves is tetramerized, the FLRT-Unc5 binding constants we observed (i.e. on the order of ~1–10 nM) are much higher than published affinities using monomeric protein in surface plasmon resonance experiments (0.3-21 μM) (Seiradake et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison of binding affinities between different assay formats, with a citation to published data.

claim: All combinations of FLRTs and Unc5s interact between opposing cells as evidenced by cell aggregation.
source: Using the cell aggregation assay, we tested every combination of FLRTs and Unc5s and found that all pairs interact between opposing cells as evidenced by cell aggregation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from cell aggregation assays shown in Figure 2D.

claim: No clusters were observed between mock transfected cells, FLRT-FLRT or Unc5-Unc5 expressing cells.
source: By contrast, no clusters were observed between mock transfected cells, FLRT-FLRT or Unc5-Unc5 expressing cells.
evidence: This is a negative control result from cell aggregation assays.

claim: Trans interactions occur between all FLRT-Unc5 pairs.
source: Together these data confirm that, as observed in our binding screen, trans interactions occur between all FLRT-Unc5 pairs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell aggregation assay results.

claim: The majority of neurons did not respond to FLRT or Unc5 stripes, growing indiscriminately across them.
source: While the majority of neurons did not respond to FLRT or Unc5 stripes, growing indiscriminately across them, we observed small populations of neurons (5-18%) that responded to FLRT1 (n=61/375, 16% attractive; n=19/375, 5% repulsive), FLRT2 (n=63/344; 18% repulsive), FLRT3 (n=37/438, 8% attractive; n=33/438, 8% repulsive), Unc5C (n=45/396, 11% repulsive) and Unc5D (n=49/407, 12% repulsive) stripes (Figure 5A-I).
evidence: This is a result from stripe assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Small populations of neurons (5-18%) responded to FLRT1, FLRT2, FLRT3, Unc5C and Unc5D stripes.
source: While the majority of neurons did not respond to FLRT or Unc5 stripes, growing indiscriminately across them, we observed small populations of neurons (5-18%) that responded to FLRT1 (n=61/375, 16% attractive; n=19/375, 5% repulsive), FLRT2 (n=63/344; 18% repulsive), FLRT3 (n=37/438, 8% attractive; n=33/438, 8% repulsive), Unc5C (n=45/396, 11% repulsive) and Unc5D (n=49/407, 12% repulsive) stripes (Figure 5A-I).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: 16% of neurons were attracted to FLRT1 stripes (n=61/375).
source: we observed small populations of neurons (5-18%) that responded to FLRT1 (n=61/375, 16% attractive; n=19/375, 5% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 5% of neurons were repelled by FLRT1 stripes (n=19/375).
source: we observed small populations of neurons (5-18%) that responded to FLRT1 (n=61/375, 16% attractive; n=19/375, 5% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 18% of neurons were repelled by FLRT2 stripes (n=63/344).
source: FLRT2 (n=63/344; 18% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 8% of neurons were attracted to FLRT3 stripes (n=37/438).
source: FLRT3 (n=37/438, 8% attractive; n=33/438, 8% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 8% of neurons were repelled by FLRT3 stripes (n=33/438).
source: FLRT3 (n=37/438, 8% attractive; n=33/438, 8% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 11% of neurons were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=45/396).
source: Unc5C (n=45/396, 11% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: 12% of neurons were repelled by Unc5D stripes (n=49/407).
source: Unc5D (n=49/407, 12% repulsive)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays.

claim: No significant response of neurons was observed to Unc5B stripes (n=3/380, 1% repulsive) relative to control laminin stripes (n=1/88, 1% repulsive).
source: No significant response of neurons was observed to Unc5B stripes (n=3/380, 1% repulsive) relative to control laminin stripes (n=1/88, 1% repulsive).
evidence: This is a negative result from stripe assays.

claim: There were no attractive or repulsive responses to Unc5A stripes (n=257/257, 100% permissive).
source: There also were no attractive or repulsive responses to Unc5A stripes (n=257/257, 100% permissive) but we did observe a modest population-wide reduction in neurite outgrowth and decreased viability (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from stripe assays.

claim: Unc5A stripes caused a modest population-wide reduction in neurite outgrowth and decreased viability.
source: There also were no attractive or repulsive responses to Unc5A stripes (n=257/257, 100% permissive) but we did observe a modest population-wide reduction in neurite outgrowth and decreased viability (data not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from stripe assays, though the data are not shown.

claim: Unc5C, Unc5D, and all three FLRTs mediate recognition events between subtypes of retinal neurons.
source: Together these data demonstrate that Unc5C, Unc5D, and all three FLRTs mediate recognition events between subtypes of retinal neurons and suggest that FLRTs and Unc5s may contribute to development of the retinal circuit.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stripe assay results.

claim: FLRTs and Unc5s may contribute to development of the retinal circuit.
source: Together these data demonstrate that Unc5C, Unc5D, and all three FLRTs mediate recognition events between subtypes of retinal neurons and suggest that FLRTs and Unc5s may contribute to development of the retinal circuit.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the functional data.

claim: All FLRT and Unc5 antibodies were highly specific with little to no cross-reactivity as assessed by ELISA using purified protein.
source: All FLRT and Unc5 antibodies were highly specific with little to no cross-reactivity as assessed by ELISA using purified protein (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a validation result shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 (note: the text says supplement 2 but the figure legend says supplement 1).

claim: At P6, FLRT1 expression was largely restricted to neurites that arborize in S1.
source: At P6 we observed laminar-restricted expression patterns for all FLRTs and three out of the four Unc5s (Figure 6). FLRT1 expression was largely restricted to neurites that arborize in S1 (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At P6, FLRT2 was most highly expressed in S2/4.
source: FLRT2 was most highly expressed in S2/4 (Figure 6B)
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At P6, FLRT3 expression was largely restricted to S3.
source: FLRT3 expression was largely restricted to S3 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6C.

claim: At P6, Unc5A was highly expressed in the cell body layers flanking the IPL and, within the IPL, was expressed in neurites that arborize in S1/2/3/5.
source: Unc5A was highly expressed in the cell body layers flanking the IPL and, within the IPL, was expressed in neurites that arborize in S1/2/3/5 (Figure 6D)
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6D.

claim: At P6, Unc5C was most highly expressed in S1/3/5.
source: Unc5C was most highly expressed in S1/3/5 (Figure 6F)
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6F.

claim: At P6, Unc5D expression was largely restricted to S1/5.
source: Unc5D expression was largely restricted to S1/5.
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining, though the specific figure reference is not provided in this sentence.

claim: At P6, Unc5B did not show laminar restriction—it was expressed at low levels uniformly across the IPL.
source: Unc5B did not show laminar restriction—it was expressed at low levels uniformly across the IPL (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Laminar-restricted expression of FLRT1-3 and Unc5A,C,D is spatio-temporally regulated.
source: Comparison of the expression patterns observed at P6 with the patterns observed at P2 and P4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2) demonstrates that laminar-restricted expression of FLRT1-3 and Unc5A,C,D is spatio-temporally regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing expression patterns across developmental time points shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: FLRT2 and Unc5C showed broad expression across the IPL at P2 that gradually became sublamina-restricted by P6.
source: One subset of proteins, FLRT2 and Unc5C, showed broad expression across the IPL at P2 that gradually became sublamina-restricted by P6.
evidence: This is a description of developmental expression patterns observed across time points.

claim: FLRT1 and FLRT3 showed sublaminar bias already at P2 that changed only slightly as the IPL expanded with age.
source: A second group, FLRT1 and FLRT3, showed sublaminar bias already at P2 that changed only slightly as the IPL expanded with age.
evidence: This is a description of developmental expression patterns observed across time points.

claim: Unc5A and Unc5D added new sublayers at later ages.
source: The final group, Unc5A and Unc5D, added new sublayers at later ages: Unc5A was not observed in the IPL until P6, even though immunoreactivity was detected in neuronal somata at earlier ages, suggesting that IPL innervation by Unc5A-positive cells happens later than other family members.
evidence: This is a description of developmental expression patterns observed across time points.

claim: Unc5A was not observed in the IPL until P6, even though immunoreactivity was detected in neuronal somata at earlier ages.
source: Unc5A was not observed in the IPL until P6, even though immunoreactivity was detected in neuronal somata at earlier ages, suggesting that IPL innervation by Unc5A-positive cells happens later than other family members.
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining across developmental time points.

claim: IPL innervation by Unc5A-positive cells happens later than other family members.
source: Unc5A was not observed in the IPL until P6, even though immunoreactivity was detected in neuronal somata at earlier ages, suggesting that IPL innervation by Unc5A-positive cells happens later than other family members.
evidence: This is an inference from the temporal expression pattern of Unc5A.

claim: Unc5D exhibited S1 restriction at P2-4 and then added expression in S5 at P6.
source: Unc5D, meanwhile, exhibited S1 restriction at P2-4 and then added expression in S5 at P6.
evidence: This is a description of developmental expression patterns observed across time points.

claim: The expression pattern of Unc5D may remain dynamic after P6, as S5 expression is maintained while S1 expression is lost by P8.
source: Interestingly, the expression pattern of Unc5D may remain dynamic after P6, as immunostaining published by Feldheim and colleagues suggests that, while S5 expression is maintained, S1 expression is lost by P8 (Sweeney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculation based on published data from another study.

claim: Between P2 and P4, Unc5C and FLRT2 expression patterns become restricted to complementary sublaminae in the IPL with Unc5C concentrated in S1/3/5 and FLRT2 predominantly expressed in S2/4.
source: Between P2 and P4, Unc5C and FLRT2 expression patterns become restricted to complementary sublaminae in the IPL with Unc5C concentrated in S1/3/5 and FLRT2 predominantly expressed in S2/4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining across developmental time points shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Complementary expression of FLRT2 and Unc5C suggests that these lamina-specific stratifications may arise due to repulsive interactions between neuronal subtypes expressing FLRT2 and Unc5C.
source: Complementary expression suggests that these lamina-specific stratifications may arise due to repulsive interactions between neuronal subtypes expressing FLRT2 and Unc5C.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the expression pattern data.

claim: Neurons repelled by Unc5C stripes expressed FLRT2 (n=26/26).
source: Neurons repelled by Unc5C stripes expressed FLRT2 (n=26/26) (Figure 5J) but not FLRT1 or FLRT3 (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining of neurons in stripe assays, shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Neurons repelled by Unc5C stripes did not express FLRT1 or FLRT3.
source: Neurons repelled by Unc5C stripes expressed FLRT2 (n=26/26) (Figure 5J) but not FLRT1 or FLRT3 (data not shown).
evidence: This is a negative result from immunostaining, though the data are not shown.

claim: Neurons repelled by FLRT2 stripes expressed Unc5C (n=30/30).
source: Conversely, neurons repelled by FLRT2 stripes expressed Unc5C (n=30/30) (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining of neurons in stripe assays, shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Interactions between FLRT2 and Unc5C induce mutual repulsion via bidirectional signaling in both the ligand- and receptor-expressing cells.
source: Together these data are consistent with a model wherein interactions between FLRT2 and Unc5C induce mutual repulsion via bidirectional signaling in both the ligand- and receptor-expressing cells.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the stripe assay and immunostaining results.

claim: Repulsive signaling of Unc5 in response to ligand binding has been well-established.
source: Repulsive signaling of Unc5 in response to ligand binding has been well-established (for review of Netrin1-induced repulsion see Moore et al., 2007; for FLRT2-induced repulsion via Unc5D see Yamagishi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited reviews and studies.

claim: All 39 neurons transfected with FLRT2-myc were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=39/328 neurons transfected).
source: We obtained 39 FLRT2-myc transfected neurons and observed that all 39 neurons were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=39/328 neurons transfected; 15 coverslips) (Figure 5L).
evidence: This is a result from gain-of-function stripe assays shown in Figure 5L.

claim: 27 out of 28 neurons that expressed Unc5C-FLAG grew permissively across Unc5C stripes (n=28/363 neurons transfected).
source: In our control transfections, we obtained 28 neurons that expressed Unc5C-FLAG and observed that 27/28 neurons grew permissively across the Unc5C stripes (n=28/363 neurons transfected; 13 coverslips) (Figure 5M).
evidence: This is a result from control gain-of-function stripe assays shown in Figure 5M.

claim: FLRT2 is sufficient to mediate repulsion in response to Unc5C.
source: These data demonstrate that FLRT2 is sufficient to mediate repulsion in response to Unc5C and, as such, repulsive signaling can occur downstream of FLRT2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gain-of-function stripe assay results.

claim: Repulsive signaling can occur downstream of FLRT2.
source: These data demonstrate that FLRT2 is sufficient to mediate repulsion in response to Unc5C and, as such, repulsive signaling can occur downstream of FLRT2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gain-of-function stripe assay results.

claim: Flrt2 is expressed by a subset of cells that includes SACs, a sparse non-SAC population in the inner nuclear layer, and a non-SAC population in the ganglion cell layer.
source: This analysis revealed that Flrt2 is expressed by a subset of cells that includes: 1) SACs; 2) a sparse non-SAC population in the inner nuclear layer (INL) (presumably amacrines due to their laminar position close to the IPL and the fact that bipolar cells are not yet born at P1); and 3) a non-SAC population in the ganglion cell layer (GCL) that, based upon their large soma size, are likely to be retinal ganglion cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a result from in situ hybridization shown in Figure 7A.

claim: At P1, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in ON SACs whose cell bodies reside in the GCL.
source: Notably, at P1, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in ON SACs whose cell bodies reside in the GCL while, at P6, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in OFF SACs whose cell bodies reside in the INL.
evidence: This is a result from in situ hybridization at P1.

claim: At P6, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in OFF SACs whose cell bodies reside in the INL.
source: Notably, at P1, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in ON SACs whose cell bodies reside in the GCL while, at P6, Flrt2 expression is predominantly detected in OFF SACs whose cell bodies reside in the INL.
evidence: This is a result from in situ hybridization at P6.

claim: About half of CART-immunoreactive cells are Flrt2-positive (n=12/23 CART+Flrt2+, n=11/23 CART+Flrt2–).
source: We observed that about half of CART-immunoreactive cells are Flrt2-positive (n=12/23 CART+Flrt2+, n=11/23 CART+Flrt2–) suggesting that a subset of ooDSGCs expresses FLRT2 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from double staining experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A subset of ooDSGCs expresses FLRT2.
source: We observed that about half of CART-immunoreactive cells are Flrt2-positive (n=12/23 CART+Flrt2+, n=11/23 CART+Flrt2–) suggesting that a subset of ooDSGCs expresses FLRT2 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is an inference from the double staining results shown in Figure 7B.

claim: tdTomato-positive SACs express FLRT2 (n=47/47).
source: Immunostaining of dissociated SACs harvested at P2 demonstrated that tdTomato-positive SACs express FLRT2 (n=47/47) but not FLRT1 (n=0/55) or FLRT3 (n=0/67) (Figure 7C-E).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining of cultured SACs shown in Figure 7C-E.

claim: tdTomato-positive SACs do not express FLRT1 (n=0/55).
source: Immunostaining of dissociated SACs harvested at P2 demonstrated that tdTomato-positive SACs express FLRT2 (n=47/47) but not FLRT1 (n=0/55) or FLRT3 (n=0/67) (Figure 7C-E).
evidence: This is a negative result from immunostaining of cultured SACs shown in Figure 7C-E.

claim: tdTomato-positive SACs do not express FLRT3 (n=0/67).
source: Immunostaining of dissociated SACs harvested at P2 demonstrated that tdTomato-positive SACs express FLRT2 (n=47/47) but not FLRT1 (n=0/55) or FLRT3 (n=0/67) (Figure 7C-E).
evidence: This is a negative result from immunostaining of cultured SACs shown in Figure 7C-E.

claim: No Unc5C expression was observed in SACs (n=0/39).
source: Indeed, while a subset of tdTomato-negative neurons were immunoreactive for Unc5C, no Unc5C expression was observed in SACs (n=0/39) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a negative result from immunostaining shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: None of the Unc5s (Unc5A, Unc5B, Unc5C, Unc5D) were expressed in SACs.
source: Furthermore, none of the other Unc5s were expressed in SACs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a negative result from immunostaining shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: 92% of SACs were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=49/53).
source: Indeed, we observed robust repulsion of SACs from Unc5C stripes (n=49/53, 92% repelled) (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from stripe assays on SACs shown in Figure 7F.

claim: 0% of SACs were repelled by FLRT2 stripes; SAC processes crossed FLRT2 stripes indiscriminately (n=71/71).
source: In contrast, SAC processes crossed FLRT2 stripes indiscriminately (n=71/71, 0% repelled) (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a negative result from stripe assays on SACs shown in Figure 7G.

claim: SAC repulsion by Unc5C could be due to interactions with FLRT2.
source: Since SACs do not express FLRT1 and FLRT3, SAC repulsion by Unc5C could be due to interactions with FLRT2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression and functional data.

claim: Repulsive FLRT2-Unc5C interactions may contribute to laminar organization of SAC neurons in the developing IPL.
source: These data suggest that repulsive FLRT2-Unc5C interactions may contribute to laminar organization of SAC neurons in the developing IPL.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the expression and functional data.

claim: Drd4-GFP ooDSGCs expressed FLRT2 and were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=7/7, 100% repelled).
source: Nevertheless, when healthy Drd4-GFP neurons were identified, we observed that they expressed FLRT2 and were repelled by Unc5C stripes (n=7/7, 100% repelled; 7 coverslips) (Figure 7H)
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining and stripe assays on Drd4-GFP neurons shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Drd4-GFP ooDSGCs were not repelled by FLRT2 stripes (n=10/10, 0% repelled).
source: but not by FLRT2 stripes (n=10/10, 0% repelled; 7 coverslips) (Figure 7I).
evidence: This is a negative result from stripe assays on Drd4-GFP neurons shown in Figure 7I.

claim: At least one subtype of DSGCs may utilize repulsive FLRT2-Unc5C interactions to achieve laminar restriction in the developing IPL.
source: These data suggest that at least one subtype of DSGCs may utilize repulsive FLRT2-Unc5C interactions to achieve laminar restriction in the developing IPL.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the Drd4-GFP neuron data.

claim: The microarray analyses were performed using neurons harvested at P6, a developmental time when extensive neurite extension, arbor refinement, laminar organization and synapse formation are occurring in the IPL.
source: The microarray analyses were performed using neurons harvested at P6, a developmental time when extensive neurite extension, arbor refinement, laminar organization and synapse formation are occurring in the IPL.
evidence: This describes the developmental stage chosen for the microarray analysis, based on knowledge of IPL development.

claim: The screen identified twenty-four previously-unreported Sema-Nrp or Sema-Plxn interactions.
source: In total, we identified twenty-four previously-unreported Sema-Nrp or Sema-Plxn interactions and confirmed four others that had been suggested by genetic interactions (see also Figure 4—source data 1 and Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the binding screen focused on Semaphorin family interactions.

claim: The screen confirmed four Sema-Nrp or Sema-Plxn interactions that had been suggested by genetic interactions.
source: In total, we identified twenty-four previously-unreported Sema-Nrp or Sema-Plxn interactions and confirmed four others that had been suggested by genetic interactions (see also Figure 4—source data 1 and Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from the binding screen that validates previously suggested interactions.

claim: Nrp1 and Nrp2 can directly interact with some members of both the Sema4 and Sema6 families.
source: Notably, we observed 1) that Nrp1 and Nrp2 can directly interact with some members of both the Sema4 and Sema6 families
evidence: This is a new finding from the binding screen.

claim: Some Sema3s can interact directly with Plxns in the absence of Nrp1 or Nrp2.
source: 2) that some Sema3s can interact directly with Plxns in the absence of Nrp1 or Nrp2 (previously only Sema3E was known to interact with PlxnD1 directly and signal in the absence of Nrp) (Gu et al., 2005)
evidence: This is a new finding from the binding screen, with a citation to previous knowledge about Sema3E.

claim: The screen identified new Sema4/5/6-Plxn interaction pairs.
source: and 3) new Sema4/5/6-Plxn interaction pairs.
evidence: This is a result from the binding screen.

claim: Different FLRT-Unc5 pairs exhibit differences in binding affinity.
source: Our experiments (Figure 2C) and those of others (Seiradake et al., 2014) have demonstrated that different FLRT-Unc5 pairs exhibit differences in binding affinity
evidence: This is a result from titration binding experiments shown in Figure 2C, also supported by cited work.

claim: Differences in binding affinity between FLRT-Unc5 pairs may contribute to recognition specificity.
source: We speculate that these differences in binding affinity contribute to recognition specificity.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of binding affinity differences.

claim: FLRT homophilic binding is difficult to detect in vitro due to very low binding affinity and is highly sensitive to experimental conditions.
source: A recent study reported that FLRT homophilic binding is difficult to detect in vitro due to very low binding affinity and is highly sensitive to experimental conditions (Seiradake et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: When measured using surface plasmon resonance, homophilic binding of FLRTs was below the sensitivity of detection (~100 μM).
source: When measured using surface plasmon resonance, homophilic binding of FLRTs was below the sensitivity of detection (~100 μM) and, in SEC-MALS experiments, a minor increase in molecular weight (from ~70 kDa to ~80 kDa) was seen with increasing concentration, but no well-defined FLRT dimer fraction was observed.
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: In SEC-MALS experiments, a minor increase in molecular weight of FLRTs (from ~70 kDa to ~80 kDa) was seen with increasing concentration, but no well-defined FLRT dimer fraction was observed.
source: When measured using surface plasmon resonance, homophilic binding of FLRTs was below the sensitivity of detection (~100 μM) and, in SEC-MALS experiments, a minor increase in molecular weight (from ~70 kDa to ~80 kDa) was seen with increasing concentration, but no well-defined FLRT dimer fraction was observed.
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: Detection of FLRT-mediated homophilic cell aggregation required five days of continuous cell shaking.
source: In addition, detection of FLRT-mediated homophilic cell aggregation required five days of continuous cell shaking, a time period considerably longer than standard protocols which typically monitor cell aggregation after shaking for 1−4 hours.
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: In crystal structures of FLRT2 and FLRT3 extracellular domains, conserved lattice contacts were observed between cis-oriented FLRT proteins.
source: In crystal structures of a portion of the FLRT2 and FLRT3 extracellular domains, conserved lattice contacts were observed between cis-oriented FLRT proteins (Seiradake et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about published structural findings from another study.

claim: Mutations at the FLRT cis-interface impaired tangential spread of pyramidal neurons between adjacent cortical columns in vivo.
source: Mutations at this interface impaired tangential spread of pyramidal neurons between adjacent cortical columns in vivo which the authors interpreted as a resulting from a defect in attractive FLRT homophilic binding.
evidence: This is a statement about published in vivo findings from another study.

claim: Binding of FLRT mutant to latrophilin is completely abolished.
source: Subsequent structural and biochemical studies by Lu et al. investigating interactions between FLRT and latrophilin, a cell surface adhesion-type G-protein-coupled receptor, demonstrated that, while the FLRT mutant exhibits a decrease in dimerization via size-exclusion gel filtration, binding of the FLRT mutant to latrophilin is completely abolished (Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: The FLRT homodimer likely occurs in cis.
source: These findings, in addition to the authors' inability to detect FLRT homophilic binding between cells, led them to conclude that the FLRT homodimer likely occurs in cis and that the in vivo pyramidal neuron phenotype may be due to a defect in FLRT-latrophilin binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion from another study, cited in the manuscript.

claim: The in vivo pyramidal neuron phenotype may be due to a defect in FLRT-latrophilin binding.
source: These findings, in addition to the authors' inability to detect FLRT homophilic binding between cells, led them to conclude that the FLRT homodimer likely occurs in cis and that the in vivo pyramidal neuron phenotype may be due to a defect in FLRT-latrophilin binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion from another study, cited in the manuscript.

claim: Latrophilins are expressed in the retina.
source: As latrophilins are expressed in the retina (Arcos-Burgos et al., 2010) (J.N.K., unpublished observations)
evidence: This is supported by a citation and unpublished observations.

claim: FLRT2 ligand binding to Unc5D-expressing pyramidal neurons modulates radial migration in the developing mouse cortex.
source: Repulsive signaling induced by FLRT2 ligand binding to Unc5D-expressing pyramidal neurons modulates radial migration in the developing mouse cortex (Yamagishi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: FLRT3 induces repulsion of Unc5B-expressing intermediate thalamic explants ex vivo.
source: Furthermore, FLRT3 induces repulsion of Unc5B-expressing intermediate thalamic explants ex vivo (Seiradake et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: Signaling downstream of Unc5B and Unc5D induces repulsion in the Unc5-expressing cell.
source: In both of these cases, neurons expressing Unc5s are repelled by FLRT ligand demonstrating that signaling downstream of Unc5 induces repulsion in the Unc5-expressing cell.
evidence: This is an inference from the cited studies.

claim: Signaling downstream of Unc5C can elicit a repulsive response.
source: Consistent with these findings, we observed that Unc5C-expressing retinal neurons are repelled by FLRT2. These data suggest that, in addition to Unc5B and Unc5D, signaling downstream of Unc5C can elicit a repulsive response.
evidence: This is an inference from the stripe assay results combined with knowledge from cited studies.

claim: A mechanism of bidirectional signaling has been well characterized between Eph receptors and their ephrin ligands.
source: A mechanism of bidirectional signaling has been well characterized between Eph receptors and their ephrin ligands (for review see Park and Lee, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited review.

claim: A mechanism of Unc5C-FLRT2 mutual repulsion would provide an elegant and efficient molecular solution for directing laminar organization/restriction of both FLRT2- and Unc5C-expressing neurons into adjacent layers during development of the IPL.
source: Such a mechanism of Unc5C-FLRT2 mutual repulsion would provide an elegant and efficient molecular solution for directing laminar organization/restriction of both FLRT2- and Unc5C-expressing neurons into adjacent layers, S2/4 and S1/3/5, respectively, during development of the IPL.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the potential functional significance of bidirectional signaling.

claim: The laminar choices of ON and OFF SACs are influenced by repulsive interactions between Plxn2 and Sema6A.
source: The laminar choices of ON and OFF SACs are influenced by repulsive interactions between Plxn2 and Sema6A (Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about published findings from another study.

claim: In PlxnA2-/- and Sema6A-/- mutants, most SAC dendrites still assemble in the correct sublamina.
source: However, in PlxnA2-/- and Sema6A-/-mutants, most SAC dendrites still assemble in the correct sublamina and even when SACs make errors they still target to S2 or S4 (Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about published genetic findings from another study.

claim: An additional molecular mechanism(s) functions in parallel to Plxn2-Sema6A to mediate precise laminar restriction of SACs.
source: This suggests that an additional molecular mechanism(s) functions in parallel to mediate precise laminar restriction of SACs.
evidence: This is an inference from the cited genetic study results.

claim: SACs and at least one subset of ooDSGCs (the Drd4-GFP population) become laminar-restricted in S2/4 due to repulsive interactions with Unc5C expressed on neighboring neurites in S1/3/5.
source: We propose that these (and perhaps other) direction-selective circuit neurons become laminar-restricted in S2/4, and/or maintain their laminar restriction once formed, due to repulsive interactions with Unc5C expressed on neighboring neurites in S1/3/5.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the expression and functional data presented.

claim: Evolution may have co-opted the same repulsive mechanism in both pre- and post-synaptic cells as a strategy for ensuring they both arborize in close spatial proximity to one another.
source: Nevertheless, our results suggest that evolution may have co-opted the same repulsive mechanism in both pre- and post-synaptic cells as a strategy for ensuring they both arborize in close spatial proximity to one another, thereby facilitating interactions between synaptic partners and limiting opportunities for inappropriate connections with neurons devoted to different visual processing tasks.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation of the findings.
